articles.title: 'Categorically false': Trump nominee fires back at report Blanche buried his secret memo
articles.description: One of President Donald Trump's last-minute judicial picks once pitched an idea inside the Justice Department that worried Attorney General Todd Blanche. The DOJ's head of the Office of Legal Counsel, T. Elliot Gaiser, proposed a memo criminalizing the shipping of abortion pills across state lines by reviving the 1873 Comstock Act, Bloomberg Law reported Tuesday. Blanche, then the deputy attorney general, nixed the idea and told Gaiser to shelve it out of fear that it would amount to a nationwide abortion ban, according to Bloomberg Law. Trump nominated Gaiser for a lifetime federal district judgeship in the Northern District of Texas. His Senate Judiciary Committee hearing is Wednesday, per Bloomberg Law. Gaiser pitched the idea during one of his first meetings with Blanche soon after he joined the DOJ in August 2025, three insider sources told Bloomberg Law. Two of the insiders said Blanche worried that the proposal would drag the Trump administration into an abortion fight that it had managed to avoid ahead of the midterms. The 1873 Comstock Act bars sending contraceptives, abortion-related items and other materials it labels obscene across state lines. According to Bloomberg Law, the law mostly sat dormant for decades before abortion opponents seized on it after the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade in 2022. One insider told Bloomberg Law that Gaiser's draft would have reached beyond banning pills to cover the transport of anything tied to abortion. A 2022 opinion from Biden's OLC found that the Comstock Act doesn't prohibit mailing abortion pills when the sender has no intent for them to be used illegally. Gaiser's memo would have undone that opinion and gone further, Bloomberg Law reported. In a phone call with Bloomberg Law, Gaiser denied its reporting shortly after it published. "Your story is categorically false, period," he said, adding that he never pushed for a nationwide abortion ban. He didn't offer Bloomberg Law any specifics on how he had presented the idea and told the outlet he generally can't discuss the advice he gives unless it becomes public.
